chunks: Death will overtake you wheresoever you be, even in the mightiest of towers. Yet if some good comes their way they say: "It is from God;" and if it is evil that befalls them, they say: "It is indeed from you." Say to them: "Every thing is from God." O, what has come upon the people that even this they fail to understand!
ai.seo_question: Why do people attribute good to God and evil to prophets or leaders according to the Quran?
ai.summary: In Shia exegesis, this verse is pivotal for understanding the balance between divine omnipotence (al-hadith) and human agency, particularly in how the Ahl al-Bayt interpret the 'good' and 'evil' mentioned. It critiques the superficial attribution of events to external causes while ignoring the deeper theological reality that all occurrences stem from Allah's will, yet requires profound insight (faqh) to truly comprehend. This highlights the necessity of deep scholarly understanding to navigate the nuances of divine decree versus human responsibility.
